entry.title: Implicit vs Explicit Learning as Teachers

link.title: Implicit vs Explicit Learning as Teachers

entry.content:
Introduction

I had 2 years experience of teaching informatics/computer science for junior high school students. After those 2 years, I started to teach English. English was my major, in fact I was majored in English language education for my bachelor and master degrees, but I think I found a critical flaw within myself as an English teacher. A kind of self-doubt, if you will.

A little bit of context, both my father and mother majored in English language education, and so am I. The difference, however, is that my parent learned English through rule-based learning while I learned English implicitly through means of real-life communication and gaming. Because of this, I remember the grammatical rules in English. For instance, I don’t remember the formula for Present Perfect Continuous tense. I also don’t know what Parts of Speech is. In fact, I have been writing all of my posts, my undergrad. thesis, master thesis, and some scientific paper without explicitly knowing the grammatical rules. I think this has something to do with how I learned the language.

In Second Language Acquisition, there are terms called explicit and implicit learning. Explicit learning is when someone actively and consciously learning the language including its rules, vocabularies, and so on, while implicit learning is when someone passively and unconsciously learning the language. All these years, since I was in the kindergarten until the moment I wrote this article, I was using implicit learning for English, and this brought up problems for me.

You see, grammar rules like tenses, parts of speech, and the likes were taught in the school. From elementary school, to junior high, and then senior high school; all of the teacher taught me the formula, but I chose to not paid attention whenever it came to English grammar rules. Almost in every English lesson given by the teachers and lecturers, I got a perfect score in all aspects. Vocabulary, perfect. Grammar, almost perfect. Text construction, perfect. In other words, I didn’t and I chose not to learn grammar explicitly, but I still aced those exercises and exams.

Only when I was assigned to teach English to 8th graders did I realize that my grammatical understanding is lacking, in terms of teaching it to the students. I understand how to construct a text, be it descriptive, expository, narrative, so on and so forth; and yet I couldn’t explain the why’s, the when’s, and the how’s of using which tenses. As such, when a teacher doesn’t possess the mastery of the fundamentals of the materials, the learning outcome(s) is bound to be not achieved.

The Action

Knowing this fatal weakness, I decided to make a deduction with a systematic approach similar to that of a Data Analyst or Scientist.

Enumerating the English Tenses

I remember that there are 16 tenses in English, all of which can be categorized into four bigger classification: Past, Present, Future, and Past-Future.

Sixteen (tenses) divided by four (classification) resulted a $4 \times 4$ combination. So, there are 4 tenses in each classification.

Then, I asked to myself:

What if the elements in each classification are similar?

To better picture my thoughts, I drew an illustration.

flowchart LR
    root((English<br/>Tenses))

    root --> present[Present]
    root --> past[Past]
    root --> future[Future]
    root --> pastfuture[Past-Future]

    present -->|Simple| present_simple[Present Simple]
    present -->|Perfect| present_perfect[Present Perfect]
    present -->|Continuous| present_continuous[Present Continuous]
    present -->|Perfect Continuous| present_perfect_continuous[Present Perfect Continuous]

    past -->|Simple| past_simple[Past Simple]
    past -->|Perfect| past_perfect[Past Perfect]
    past -->|Continuous| past_continuous[Past Continuous]
    past -->|Perfect Continuous| past_perfect_continuous[Past Perfect Continuous]

    future -->|Simple| future_simple[Future Simple]
    future -->|Perfect| future_perfect[Future Perfect]
    future -->|Continuous| future_continuous[Future Continuous]
    future -->|Perfect Continuous| future_perfect_continuous[Future Perfect Continuous]

    pastfuture -->|Simple| pastfuture_simple[Past-Future Simple]
    pastfuture -->|Perfect| pastfuture_perfect[Past-Future Perfect]
    pastfuture -->|Continuous| pastfuture_continuous[Past-Future Continuous]
    pastfuture -->|Perfect Continuous| pastfuture_perfect_continuous[Past-Future Perfect Continuous]

    classDef cls fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#1e3a8a
    classDef tense fill:#f1f5f9,stroke:#64748b,color:#0f172a
    class present,past,future,pastfuture cls
    class present_simple,present_perfect,present_continuous,present_perfect_continuous,past_simple,past_perfect,past_continuous,past_perfect_continuous,future_simple,future_perfect,future_continuous,future_perfect_continuous,pastfuture_simple,pastfuture_perfect,pastfuture_continuous,pastfuture_perfect_continuous tense

Using this model, we only need to remember or understand as few as 6 nodes.

  • Past
  • Present
  • Future

… for the time dimension; and …

  • Simple
  • Perfect
  • Continuous

… for the circumstance dimension; and also …

  • Past-Future combination
  • Perfect Continuous combination

I do understand that excluding the last two nodes feels like cheating the number to make a “bait” for everyone. But, in my defense, they are just combinations of the existing nodes in each respective dimension. So, it wouldn’t occupy much of your brain memory, would it?

Discussion with Peers

I have some friends who are willing to discuss with me about English. They are my classmates. And, funily enough, one of them had the same problem with me. She realized that a portion of her knowledge about English grammar is based on “feelings” rather than the rule itself. Therefore, we discussed from the very foundation of the English language, the Parts of Speech. Luckily, she was a teaching assistant in a university in 2022, and she still have some General English materials saved in her device’s storage.

When I was trying to comprehend the Parts of Speech, something came up to my mind. A refletive question for myself.

I learned English implicitly and thus I couldn’t teach English maximally; do teachers who learned implicitly also struggle to teach what they learned?

To answer this question, I prepared a mini research, which is elaborated in a different section.

Self-study

For the past few years, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic emerged globally, my learning style had shifted quite radically. I went from instructor-led learning to self-paced learning. I felt the effectiveness of self-paced learning significanly inclining after I learned (1) Google Dorking technique from a cybersecurity bootcamp on Q2 2025, and (2) started playing Arknights: Endfield on Q1 2026, where the latter being the most impactful catalyst that shaped my engineering mindset.

You might wonder the correlation between learning style and engineering mindset I mentioned earlier. Well, there is a reciprocal relationship between the two. First, I see engineering as a state of mind rather than a formal education faculty. This means that engineering mindset is not exclusive to those who studied engineering, anyone who is crafty and curious enough can have this mindset, and so I believe. With this engineering mindset that I developed from playing Arknights: Endfield, I constantly thinking of ways to circumvent all kinds of problem, including “engineering” the way I learn. In educational sciences, this experience is recognized as meta-cognition. It is the ability when someone thinks about thinking. In other words, I hacked my own brain to learn faster by using meta-cognition.

As of the writing of this article (2026-10-27 22:06:00 +0700), I have learned half of the Parts of Speech.

entry.title: Found bug in Indonesia’s Ministry of Education’s Software Installer

link.title: Found bug in Indonesia’s Ministry of Education’s Software Installer

entry.content:
Introduction

I’m enrolled in a teacher professional program from Indonesia government. At the end of the program, there is an exam. When I took the program, the exam was online from home, and we had to install a specific software, most of the time it’s called “exambrowser”. But some bugs prevented me and the other participants to download and install the software.

I’m going to tell it in chronological order just like a report.

URL Analysis

On 18th of October 2026, I received a notification from the program administrator (from the university) that all participants to download the exambrowser for final exam. This was where my analyst instinct kicked in. The administrator (or perhaps more of a manager or coordinator) of the program sent a link to the exambrowser software. The link was referring to a subdomain of kemdikbud (previous nomenclature for Ministry of Education) while in fact the ministry changed name since the new president ruled. The ministry changed name from Kemdikbudristekdikti to Kemendikdasmen (for primary and secondary education) and Kemendiktisaintek (for higher education and research). The link, of course, returned an error. It couldn’t be accessed.

[omitted]

Windows:
http://exam.bppp.kemdikbud.go.id/win

Mac:
http://exam.bppp.kemdikbud.go.id/mac

[omitted]

I found two problems here. The network protocol is in http when it should usually be in https. The former being insecure connection and the latter is a secured connection protocol for http network transfer. The second problem was the domain name. It should be *.kemendikdasmen.go.id instead of *.kemdikbud.go.id.

To test it, I opened the link for Windows and (you guessed it!) it returned an error of “expired server certificate”.

As a work around, I changed the link to use the new ministry domain. And, sure enough, it worked and a download started.

The Exambrowser Installer

The downloaded software turned out to be an installer instead of the program itself. I didn’t think much that time so I ran the program. It tried to fetch the “real” exambrowser but apparently the installer returned a “download error” and that I need to check my internet connection. This was ridiculous because my internet connection was not to blame. Good internet connection from the ISP, even from two different VPN provider. Despite many alternatives, the installer refused to continue and showed the same error again and again.

I consulted to the video tutorial on how to install the exambrowser installer (*insert yo dawg meme). I know, I know. For an IT practicioner like me to watch a video on how to install a software is kind of awkward and embarrassing, but hey, I know my stuff alright.

The video showed the installer “downloading exambrowser…” status log. This is a huge evidence that the software I installed was actually an online installer, not a standalone installer. It’s like when you install a browser for a newly born PC. You download, say, “internet_browser.exe” but it turned out it’s an online installer and not a standalone installer. This case was the same. But this part of information became a crucial turning point for my investigation.

Now I knew that the software fetches the installer from the ministry’s server, and then installs the exambrowser on the client PC. But what if I told you that the online installer fetches from the wrong address? I mean, when the ministry name changed, the domain name for that ministry have to be changed too. Well, they didn’t. At that time.

Network Analysis using Wireshark

My hypothesis was that the online installer fetches from the wrong address. To prove this, I used wireshark to see where this “online installer” is fetching from.

Network connection captured when the Online Installer "start to Install" the exambrowser.

Also check the .pcap file for yourself if you are curious like me.

It is evident that the online installer fetches from *.kemdikbud.go.id and not *.kemendikdasmen.go.id.

I reported this to the administrator to be relayed to the IT dept in Ministry of Education.

By the way, in all of my post, I use Ministry of Education or Ministry of Higher Education instead of whatever the ministry name is at the moment. I hate when the ministry name is always changing. It confuses the hell out of people (go make up your mind, dear oh so distinguished Mr. or Mrs. President of Indonesia. Like, seriously.)

Follow up

The online installer has been fixed on 19th of October 2026.
entry.summary: Surface level Reverse Engineering with Network Flow using Wireshark

entry.title: Understanding by Design: An Approach to Lesson Planning

link.title: Understanding by Design: An Approach to Lesson Planning

entry.content:
Introduction

This article is dedicated to one of the assignments from Teacher Professional Program. I’m writing this as a student of Universitas Galuh.

We, the students, were given a topic about lesson plan principle entitled “Understanding by Design” (also known as Backward Design).

This approach highlights seven points:

  1. Clear learning objectives
  2. Applicability into real life
  3. Measurable comprehension (through explanation, analysis, application, perspective, empathize, or reflection)
  4. Informs curriculum design
  5. Ensures learning happens
  6. Evaluative properties
  7. Anchors continuous development

These points can be optimally implemented using the following step:

  1. Determine the learning objectives
  2. Design the assessment
  3. Choose the activities

Analysis

This part discusses the implementation of the backward design in my previous lesson plans.

Historically speaking, the way I design my lesson have always been revolving around applicability. I focused on how a particular material is important for the students to learn and how can the students use the knowledge in real life situations. As an example, I taught “data analysis” to 8th grade students (previously I was Informatics teacher due to reasons) and how analyzing information they already have can help them in life.

I designed the materials in such a way that I proposed many questions to the students about the essence of Mathematics. This was done so that the students could be more aware of what can be done by simple math. Simple counting, data aggregation, and arithmatics. One of the example is to see how much something has progressed by using a simple division aritmatics. I told my students that communicating with raw numbers might distort how people perceive the main idea. Therefore, we use a standardized scale to perceive the progress of something.

entry.title: 6. Nonrelational Databases
entry.content:
Introduction

This is a post about my assignment submission from Microsoft’s Data Science for Beginner Repository. This assignment is about performing calculation on a dataset.

Assignment

  1. Calculate the Gross profits of FY ‘15, ‘16, ‘17, and ‘18
  2. Calculate the average of all the gross profits (Sum of gross profits divided by number of fiscal years [10])

Submission

Q1

The formula for Gross Profit is Net operating revenue - Cost of goods sold. First, do for one column using the following formula:

=I4-I5

Then, Autofill to the right side.

Q2

Returning the Mean of Gross profit is straightforward. Sum all up then divide it by the count of numbers. It can be achieved quicker using the following formula:

=AVERAGE(C6:L6)

entry.title: 5. Relational Databases
entry.content:
Introduction

This post is my assignment submission from Microsoft’s Data Science for Beginners Repository. The assignment is about “Displaying Airport Data” using SQLite. As instructed, I’m using SQLite extension that is installed inside VSCode.

Assignment

  1. all city names in the Cities table
  2. all cities in Ireland in the Cities table
  3. all airport names with their city and country
  4. all airports in London, United Kingdom

Q1

SELECT city
FROM Cities;

Q2

SELECT city
FROM Cities
WHERE country = 'Ireland'

Q3

SELECT Airports.name, Cities.city, Cities.country
FROM Cities
RIGHT JOIN Airports
  ON Airports.city_id = Cities.city;

Q4

SELECT name
FROM Airports
WHERE city_id = (SELECT id FROM Cities WHERE city = 'London');

entry.title: 1.1 Defning Data Science
entry.content:
Introduction

This is a post about my assignment submission from Microsoft’s Data Science for Beginners repository. Specifically, this is submission for the first lesson.

Problems

  1. How can you use data to improve education process for children in schools?
  2. How can you use data to control vaccination during the pandemic?
  3. How can you use data to make sure you are being productive at work?

Answer

Prior to giving my answer, I would like to justify that filling the assignment using table format while I write it on raw markdown may render my work excessively time consuming. Therefore, I’m writing it in list format.

Education

Student’s comprehension level

  • Data collection: pre-test, post-test, exercises, mid-term exam, final-term exam
  • Data storage: Microsoft Excel, Google Spreadsheet, DBMS, CSV
  • Insights: Teaching approach, teaching strategy, teaching methodology, curriculum development, test design, option distractors, item difficulty index (for multiple choice)

Teacher Likability

  • Data collection: Student’s presence list (daily), Teacher presence list
  • Data storage: Microsoft Excel, Google Spreadsheet, DBMS, CSV
  • Insights: Student’s most anticipated teacher, teacher professional development

Test Quality

  • Data collection: mid-term exam, final-term exam
  • Data storage: Microsoft Excel, Google Spreadsheet, DBMS, CSV
  • Insights: Test quality, curriculum development, item analysis (distractor, discriminiation index, difficulty index)

Vaccination

Vaccination Survey

  • Data collection: Identification number, vaccination date
  • Data storage: Paper-based logs, Microsoft Excel, Google Spreadsheet, DBMS, CSV
  • Insights: Monitoring which state/region have lower number of vaccinated person

Vaccine Effectivity

  • Data collection: Patient ID, Patient basic information, vaccination status, vaccination date, symptoms, status (deceased/alive)
  • Data storage: Strict DBMS
  • Insights: Confidence level of the vaccine curing the virus.

Vaccine Side Effects

  • Data collection: Patient ID, Patient basic information, vaccination status, vaccination date, symptoms, status (deceased/alive)
  • Data storage: Strict DBMS
  • Insights: Vaccine improvements, vaccine dosage, vaccine terms of use(?)

Productivity

Employee Performance

  • Data collection: Employee ID, Employee Department, Employee Job Role, KPI, Target Achieved (boolean)
  • Data storage: Strict company DBMS
  • Insights: HR decision to train employee

Employee Churn Rate

  • Data collection: Employee ID, Employee Department, Employee Job Role, KPI, Target Achieved (boolean), Employee Presence List
  • Data storage: Strict company DBMS
  • Insights: HR decision to make new reward system

entry.title: 2. Intro to GitHub
entry.content:
Introduction

This is a post about my learning into Web Dev for Beginners from Microsoft. It contains my reflections, notes, and many more.

First Repository Check-in: How Did That Feel?

How did it feel to see your code appear on GitHub for the first time?

My first ever commit to GitHub was long ago, about 1 to 2 years ago. But honestly, it felt like I was a true developer! The feeling of successfully committing my very first code into my GitHub repository was amazing. I can’t believe with my very own eyes that I could do what other developers can do. Nowadays, as my commit increase largely, I feel accustomed to git push and pull. Although I think I still touching the surface of Git. There are so many commands which function is unknown to me. That is why I think this course is good for me to get to know better about Git.

Which step felt the most confusing, and which felt surprisingly easy?

The most confusing part was when I was first trying it back then. Everything felt alien even for making an empty directory and the .gitignore felt hard. But as I used more and more git commands, it became second nature, really. Especially when I learned more about Linux and the terminal. All those frustrations getting to know Linux paid off now.

Can you explain the difference between git add, git commit, and git push in your own words?

git add is when we want to stage the file(s) or folder(s) of your selection. We can add the whole directory along with its sub directories using the dot .; or we can specify it to a directory or file (but this one takes very long time to do, even more when you have many files to commit).

git commit is a required command to execute after we perform git add. It is a command to give notes to our file(s) and folder(s) in the staging. I still don’t know why it is a must, though. Maybe it has something to do with hashing?

git push is when we want to send the file(s) and folder(s) in our staging into the cloud/GitHub. It’s very straightforward. We push what we have in the staging into our GitHub repository of choice. What I mean by “of choice” is that GitHub allow collaboration, so it can be your own repository or even someone else’s. I read that collaboration is next in the sub chapter so I will stop here.

Collaboration Skills Check: Ready to Work With Others?

Does the idea of forking and pull requests make sense to you now?

Quite. Forking is when we want to copy other’s repository into our profile. For example, person A created a repo called “Website Project 1”, but person A worked in collaboration with person B and C. Person B and person C need to have the same draft from person A (let’s just assume that person A is the leader). Just like in a writing collaboration project where everyone write on the same paper (well, that would be chaotic, to be honest), but instead of in one paper we copy the draft so that everyone got one copy. This is called “fork”. It’s like asking and getting the exact copy of somneone else’s repository.

Pull Request (shorthand: PR) has quite the confusing term. It’s “pull” but not to our local machine. I mean, we use git pull to get changes from main branch into our local machine, right? But PR is actually comes from other contributors. If we use the context in the previous example, and let’s say that person B made changes inside their branch and want to push it to the main branch (of the repo created by person A). Person B need to conduct Pull Request. It’s like telling person A and person C that person B made some changes and want everyone to apply it in their working space.

What’s one thing about working with branches that you want to practice more?

I think I want to practice more about collaborating in general. I get the idea of collaborating in GitHub is quite the same with collaborating with people in Google Docs or other real-time document editing platform. The difference being that GitHub is not quite that real-time, and that we are working in a copy of the main draft. That said, I think I need to find some friends who are willing to collaborate with me. About coding, that is.

How comfortable do you feel about contributing to someone else’s project?

I love helping others. But now, I think my skill in coding is not enough for collaboration. I mean, I’m still beginner at coding or developing a system or anything, and people are already making good and awesome projects. So, for the time being, I will work alone. I have a friend who is willing to learn code but she seems to be busy with her businesses.

Testing Skill Check: Ready to Find Issues?

Which testing method seems most approachable to you right now?

I think the screen reader is the most approachable right now. I myself have a visual impairment. I have Stargardt disease (low vision). I navigate mostly using keyboard now, although sometimes I still use mouse. When gaming, I also prefer to use a controller than a keyboard and mouse (previously the opposite).

Can you imagine using keyboard-only navigation for a full day?

Actually, I’m doing it right now. Navigating through keyboard and keystrokes. It’s actually faster for me because I have a visual impairment.

What’s one accessibility barrier you’ve personally experienced online?

Thanks to my disability, I find it hard to see screen in bright environment. Small texts are hard to read. And also there is this blind spots around my central vision that prevent me from seeing whatever lies beneath it.

POUR Principles Check: Making It Stick

Can you think of a website feature that fails each POUR principle?

A website that violates each of POUR princple. I will start with the P first.

  • Perceivable: A website that don’t give alt text to media.
  • Operable: A website that can only accept mouse pointer input, neglecting keyboard input.
  • Understandable: A website that is meant for middle schoolers but the content of the posts used university-level vocabulary.
  • Robust: A website that is only designed specifically for a certain device, say, PCs only; Users with small screen (smartphones) will struggle to see or even understand the website.

Which principle feels most natural to you as a developer?

I would say Understandable and Robust are the “must have” features of a website.

How might these principles improve design for everyone, not just disabled users?

People may need accessibility features even if they don’t have any disabilities. For example, people who is reading an email in bright sunlight (let’s just say that this person is outdoor) may struggle to read the screen because the light of the screen is lower than the light of the sun. This will make the screen look dark and hard to see, not to mention read the texts inside that little screen.

Semantic HTML Mastery Check: Building Strong Foundations

Can you identify the landmarks on a webpage just by looking at the HTML?

Yes. Landmarks are usually inside a <nav> HTML element.

How would you explain the difference between <section> and <div> to a friend?

The difference between <section> and <div> lies in the compliance. Div is like the general purpose tag. You can use it literally for anything you like. But that leaves problems. If everything is built upon the div tag, you wouldn’t know which one is which. As a developer, I see this as a nightmare. Hard to read. The section tag on the other hand tells us that what lies inside the tag is actually a part of the main content of the page. You wouldn’t place a section tag in the navigation tag, would you? Or in the buttons. So, section tag is actually behaves just like the div tag but it has semantic features that helps differentiate which tag is which and belong to which element group. Using section tag in the main body of the content is considered best practice, but you can still use div for other parts of the webpage.

What’s the first thing you’d check if a screen reader user reported navigation problems?

I would check the HTML tag used in the HTMl document. First, I would ask which specific part is the problem. Users may not be proficient enough in reading HTML so I would ask for which part of the content. From there, I would backtrack which tag is that paragraph or content is from.

entry.title: Maintenance Rumah dan Fisika
entry.content:
Sekilas

Menguras toren cara cepat menggunakan Fisika:

Gambar 1. Xyphon untuk Membersihkan dan Menguras Toren.

Pengantar

Pada 1 September 2026, air PDAM ke rumah saya kecil bahkan mati karena ada kegiatan kemah di bagian barat Desa Sadamantra. Perkemahan tersebut menyita pasokan air untuk masyarakat yang ada di wilayah timur desa. Sebagai konteks, bagian barat mendekati naik ke gunung Ciremai.

Ketika menyalakan pompa air dari sumur, pompanya tidak menyala karena suatu masalah. Penjelasan masalah tersebut ada di artikel sebelumnya.

Sekitar sepekan kemudian, 8 September 2026, volume air di toren kami habis. Ini kesempatan yang bagus untuk menguras toren karena di bawah nya sudah banyak endapan. Saya rasa endapan tersebut adalah kapur karena warnanya yang putih keruh.

Teknik

Untuk membersihkan endapan dan menguras toren kami, saya mengusulkan untuk menggunakan konsep Siphon (Xyphon) yang ada di ilmu fisika. Hal ini saya usulkan karena tidak memungkinkan bagi orang untuk masuk ke dalam toren lalu menggayung air seember-seember.

“Daripada bekerja keras, lebih baik bekerja cerdas”, pikir saya.

Usulan awal saya yaitu menggunakan konsep fisika, namun pada saat itu saya belum tau nama spesifik dari mekanisme fluida tersebut. Saya konsultasikan ke beberapa sumber yang salah dua diantaranya adalah lulusan Magister Pendidikan Fisika dan video YouTube Michael (Vsauce).

Setelah mengumpulkan informasi, saya mendapatkan bahwa konsep fisika yang relevan adalah gravitasi, tekanan hidrostatis, dan hukum Bernoulli.

Ide utamanya adalah air akan selalu mengalir ke permukaan yang lebih rendah. Hal ini disebabkan semakin dekat jarak relatif suatu lubang menuju inti bumi (gravitasi) maka tekanan yang ditimbulkan pun akan semakin besar.

Eksperimen

Sebagai proof-of-concept, saya memutuskan untuk mencoba konsep Xyphon ini menggunakan peralatan dapur. Diantaranya, gelas, sedotan, dan air.

(Video menyusul)

Eksekusi

Kami menyediakan selang yang panjangnya lebih dari 2 kali tinggi toren.
